thread:
Maria: customers on dedicated/private stacks are seeing 401s from our auth sidecar. they claim client certs are sent by the LB but auth logs show none

Dave: which topology? NLB/ALB -> istio gateway -> sidecar? or straight proxy?

Maria: customer-managed ALB terminates mTLS, forwards to istio-ingressgateway, then to our sidecar. they used to emit a header with the client cert. now 401s.

Ryan: quick sanity: confirm LB is still re-emitting the cert header, and whether istio is configured to preserve that header. istio can drop headers considered sensitive.

Maria: repro curl I ran:
```
curl -v https://dedicated-cust.svc.redwood.net/health --cert test-client.pem --key test-client.key -H "Host: cust.local"
```
sidecar: `authz: missing client cert header, deny 401`

Ingrid: which header name are they using? X-CLIENT-CERT vs X-REDWOOD-CLIENT-CERT? casing/length matters. Also LB may base64 or PEM encode.

Maria: they were using X-CLIENT-CERT (PEM block). our sidecar accepts either but expects base64 DER ideally.

Dave: another possibility: the ingressgateway has an HTTP filter that normalizes or strips long headers. check gateway `proxyConfig` and `envoy` filters.

Maria: I ran tcpdump at the LB->ingress interface and saw X-CLIENT-CERT present. tcpdump on pod interface (post-ingress) shows header missing. so istio is the likely dropper.

Ryan: check the istio ingressgateway deployment args for `--envoy-disable-extension-xyz` or any `header_sanitizer` plugin. also look for an `EnvoyFilter` the customer installed.

Maria: the customer had a 3rd-party WAF annotation on the istio service. removing it made the header pass but they need the WAF.

Ingrid: workaround we used before: an EnvoyFilter on the gateway that reads downstream TLS metadata and sets a safe header (X-REDWOOD-CLIENT-CERT-B64) from `%DOWNSTREAM_PEER_CERT%`, plus a small lua script to base64 the cert if needed.

Dave: sample Lua snippet (very short):
```lua
function envoy_on_request(request_handle)
  local cert = request_handle:streamInfo():downstreamSslConnection():getPeerCertificates()[0]
  if cert then
    request_handle:headers():add("x-redwood-client-cert-b64", cert:toDer():base64())
  end
end
```

Ryan: if customer can't run that, ask LB team to set `preserve_client_cert=true` and re-emit header to ingress with a short alias name. warn them about header length limits.

Maria: applied EnvoyFilter with Lua on their gateway and auth passed (200s). documented the filter for them.

eng-infra-bot: created SUPPORT-7421 to track: ingress header sanitization causing mTLS mapping failures

Ingrid: follow-ups:
- eng-infra: add KB for istio gateway header passthrough + Lua/EnvoyFilter examples (Dave)
- eng-runtime: add fallback to accept `x-forwarded-client-cert` and `ssl-client-cert` artifacts in sidecar, and support PEM/base64 variants (Ryan)
- support: add tcpdump + http echo probe steps to triage (Maria)

Maria: pushed repro logs and tcpdump snippets to ticket. customer agreed to the EnvoyFilter workaround for now. closing this Slack thread once KB is up. :thumbsup:

Ryan: note for KB: mention header encoding, max header length, and that some istio filters (and WAFs) intentionally strip `X-` headers. include troubleshooting checklist: tcpdump upstream, tcpdump post-ingress, pod echo, check gateway `EnvoyFilter` list, check service annotations.

Dave: I'll draft the KB and share in eng-infra docs for review.

Maria: thanks everyone."
